reaction: The everyday counterexample makes the limitation clear.
reason: This is the only offered combination and addresses how another workshop can obtain the method.

effect: The printed instructions make the method available for inspection and trial elsewhere, without establishing that anyone repeated it successfully. Both goals are complete.
reaction: The distinction between circulating a method and verifying its results is useful.

mostWorthwhile.text: Testing the initial heat–light link against moonlight and rubbing was most worthwhile: the contrasting cases showed why supporting examples alone are insufficient.

leastWorthwhile.text: Printing the instructions was relevant, but it felt less interactive than comparing the cases; it was also the only combination offered at that point.

surprise.text: The moonlight result distinguished little noticeable warmth from no energy transfer, a useful qualification.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though the connection between contested printing and trial instructions was broad rather than a detailed account of publication.

continue.text: Yes. I would try another chapter for the concise comparisons and careful limits on what the evidence establishes, though the compatible-choice menu leaves little discovery of combinations.
